items.title: Continuous periodic solenoidal surrogate residual
items.design_state: Step 1 draft; continuous residual definition authored against the current Fourier and Leray interfaces.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, $T>0$, and $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ with normalized volume $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. For a vector field $w$, use the componentwise Fourier coefficients $\widehat w(k)=\int_{Q_d}w(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$ and norm $\|w\|_2=(\int_{Q_d}|w(x)|^2\,d\mu(x))^{1/2}$. Define $P_0=I$ and, for $k\ne0$, $P_k=I-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2$, with $\widehat{Pw}(k)=P_k\widehat w(k)$; $P$ is the Leray projector. For a smooth spatial vector field $w:Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$, define $\operatorname{div}w(x)=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jw_j(x)$; for a smooth time-dependent vector field $w:[0,T]\times Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$, define $\operatorname{div}w(t,x)=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jw_j(t,x)$, with derivatives taken only in $x$; for a tensor field $F=(F_{ij})$, set $(\operatorname{div}F)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jF_{ij}$, and set $(v\otimes v)_{ij}=v_i v_j$. Let $\Delta=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_j^2$. A smooth spatial field $w:Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$ is solenoidal, or divergence-free, iff $\operatorname{div}w(x)=0$ for every $x\in Q_d$; a smooth time-dependent field $w:[0,T]\times Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$ is solenoidal iff $\operatorname{div}w(t,x)=0$ for every $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times Q_d$. Given a constant $\nu\ge0$, smooth $f:[0,T]\times Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$, a smooth solenoidal field $v:[0,T]\times Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$, and a smooth solenoidal reference initial field $u_0:Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$, define the continuous residual and initial defect by

$$r_v:=\partial_t v+P\operatorname{div}(v\otimes v)-\nu\Delta v-Pf,\qquad d_0:=\|v(0,\cdot)-u_0\|_2.$$

The residual is a continuous function of time with values in $L^2(Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$, so $\int_0^T\|r_v(t,\cdot)\|_2\,dt$ is finite. This is a continuous-domain residual: finitely many collocation values do not by themselves bound this $L^1_tL^2_x$ quantity. All quantities here are mathematical; no physical units are assigned to $\nu$.

items.title: Lipschitz observable bias under bounded law shift
items.design_state: Step 1 draft; repaired statistical supplier and final drained observable-law interfaces checked; authoring readiness current; independent review pending.
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal Z,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space and let $\mu$ be a probability measure on it, meaning a countably additive measure on $\Sigma$ with $\mu(\mathcal Z)=1$. Let $X$ be a real normed vector space and give it the norm-Borel $\sigma$-algebra generated by its norm-open sets. Let $S,\widetilde S:\mathcal Z\to X$ be measurable maps. Let $J:X\to\mathbb R$ be $L$-Lipschitz, meaning $|J(x)-J(y)|\le L\|x-y\|_X$ for all $x,y\in X$, with $L\ge0$. Suppose

$$\int_{\mathcal Z}\bigl(\|S\|_X^2+\|\widetilde S\|_X^2\bigr)\,d\mu<\infty,\qquad \int_{\mathcal Z}\|S-\widetilde S\|_X^2\,d\mu\le\varepsilon^2$$

for some finite $\varepsilon\ge0$. For a measurable scalar function $h$, write $\|h\|_{L^2(\mu)}=(\int_{\mathcal Z}|h|^2\,d\mu)^{1/2}$. Let $g:\mathcal Z\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable with $\int g\,d\mu=1$ and $g\le C$ $\mu$-almost everywhere for a finite $C\ge1$, and define the target probability law by $\nu(E)=\int_Eg\,d\mu$ for $E\in\Sigma$, with target expectation $\mathbb E_\nu[H]=\int Hg\,d\mu$ whenever the integral exists. Then the measurable scalar observables $J\circ S$ and $J\circ\widetilde S$ are $\nu$-integrable and

$$\left|\mathbb E_\nu[J(S)]-\mathbb E_\nu[J(\widetilde S)]\right|\le L\sqrt C\,\varepsilon.$$

The estimate assumes a population mean-square error under $\mu$ and a bounded target density $g$; a finite test sample by itself establishes neither assumption. The state space may represent fluid fields when that measurable state model is supplied. For a physical application, both observables must use the same declared scalar unit; this mathematical proposition assigns no physical units.

items.title: Unseen input invalidates a training-law guarantee
items.design_state: Step 1 draft; repaired statistical supplier and final drained observable-law interfaces checked; authoring readiness current; independent review pending.
items.statement:
Let $d_s=2$, $D=(0,1)^2$, and $I=[0,1]$. Let $X$ consist of the constant product-measurable fields $c e_1:D	imes I	o\mathbb R^2$, where $c\in\mathbb R$ and $e_1=(1,0)$, with norm $\|c e_1\|_X=|c|$ and its Borel $\sigma$-algebra; thus $X$ is isometric to $\mathbb R$ and is a separable real Banach space. Let $Z=\{0,1\}$ with its power-set $\sigma$-algebra and define $S(z)=0$, $\widetilde S(0)=0$, $\widetilde S(1)=M e_1$ for arbitrary $M>0$, and $J(c e_1)=c$, which is $1$-Lipschitz. An $X$-valued simple map means a map with finite range and measurable fibers. A map is strongly measurable with respect to a probability law if, outside a measurable set of measure zero, it is a pointwise norm limit of a sequence of simple maps. Here $S$ and $\widetilde S$ are themselves simple maps, so their constant approximating sequences establish strong measurability for either law below. For $z\in Z$, define the Dirac law $\delta_z$ by $\delta_z(E)=1$ if $z\in E$ and $0$ otherwise. Take training law $\mu=\delta_0$ and target law $
u=\delta_1$. Then the training-law mean-square state error is zero, while the target-law observable bias is $M$. Absolute continuity $
u\ll\mu$ means that $\mu(E)=0$ implies $
u(E)=0$ for every measurable $E\subseteq Z$. The target law is not absolutely continuous with respect to the training law, so the bounded-density hypothesis of the shift certificate fails; as $M$ is arbitrary, training-law error alone supplies no finite uniform target-bias bound.
